note: Always s, and only before ‹a›, ‹o› or ‹u›: ‹o açúcar›, oo ah-SOO-kahr.
Always s, never z: ‹a pessoa›, ah peh-SOH-uh. A single ‹s› between vowels is z: ‹a casa›.
‹g› before ‹e› or ‹i› sounds zh: ‹a página›, ah PAH-zhee-nuh. Before ‹a›, ‹o› or ‹u› it is a hard g: ‹a garrafa›.
The ‹u› is usually silent and keeps the ‹g› hard: ‹a guerra›, ah GHEH-huh.
Usually sh: ‹a caixa›, ah KAI-shuh. In some words it is ks (‹o táxi›, oo TAHK-see), z (‹o exame›) or s (‹próximo›).
A stressed ah: ‹o cardápio›, oo kahr-DAH-pyoo.
An open eh, as in bet, and stressed: ‹o café›, oo kah-FEH.
A closed ay, and stressed: ‹você›, voh-SAY.
A stressed ee: ‹a família›, ah fah-MEE-lyuh.
An open aw, as in law, and stressed: ‹a avó›, ah ah-VAW.
A closed oh, and stressed: ‹o avô›, oo ah-VOH.
A stressed oo: ‹o açúcar›, oo ah-SOO-kahr.
‹g› before ‹e› is zh; ‹en› before a consonant is nasal; final ‹te› is chee. Ends in ‹e›: stress on the next-to-last syllable.
‹h› is silent; final ‹l› is w. Ends in ‹l›: stress on the last syllable.
‹r› after ‹p› is a quick tap; ‹ai› as in eye; final ‹a› is a weak uh. Ends in ‹a›: stress on the next-to-last syllable.
‹ç› is s; ‹c› before ‹a› is k. The accent mark puts the stress on ‹ú›.
‹ai› as in eye; ‹x› is sh. Ends in ‹a›: stress on the next-to-last syllable.
‹r› at the end of a syllable changes by region; final ‹te› is chee. Ends in ‹e›: stress on the next-to-last syllable.
‹nh› is ny; ‹ã› is nasal, and the syllable with the tilde takes the stress.
‹ão› is nasal, owng, and the syllable with the tilde takes the stress.
‹g› before ‹a› is hard; ‹rr› is h. Ends in ‹a›: stress on the next-to-last syllable.
‹j› is zh; ‹an› before a consonant is nasal. Ends in ‹r›: stress on the last syllable.
‹é› is an open eh and takes the stress; ‹d› before ‹i› is j; final ‹o› is oo.
‹ô› is a closed oh and takes the stress; final ‹s› stays s.
‹ú› takes the stress; ‹s› between vowels is z; ‹c› before ‹a› is k.
‹g› before ‹e› is zh; final ‹em› is nasal, ayng. Ends in ‹em›: stress on the next-to-last syllable.
‹ch› is sh; final ‹a› is a weak uh. Ends in ‹a›: stress on the next-to-last syllable.
‹lh› is ly. Ends in ‹r›: stress on the last syllable.
‹an› before a consonant is nasal; final ‹de› is jee. Ends in ‹e›: stress on the next-to-last syllable.
